newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CLP, Exxon sign China power plant JV.
newsitem.headline: CLP, Exxon sign China power plant JV.

text.p: China Light and Power Co Ltd said on Thursday it had signed a joint venture agreement with Exxon Energy Ltd and several joint venture partners for the development of a 1,050-megawatt gas-fired power plant project in China's Shenzhen.
Exxon Energy is a subsidiary of Exxon Corp of Texas.

The agreement was signed in Shenzhen, neighbouring Hong Kong, by China Light's wholly-owned China Energy Investment Co Ltd, Exxon Energy, Shenzhen Qianwan Electric Power Development Co Ltd, Guangdong Electric Power Holdings Co and Kanematsu Power (South China) Co Ltd, the statement said.

China Light said the signing of the agreement would pave the way for negotiation of the detailed terms of the venture and the resupply of gas for the project, subject to approval by the Chinese central government and other authorities.
A memorandum of understanding between the joint venture partners was signed in October.

Under the joint venture agreement, China Light's unit and Exxon Energy will each have a 17.5 percent interest in the project, Kanematsu Power at 29 percent, and the other two Chinese partners will have 36 percent interest, it said.

The power project will consist of three units of 350-megawatt class combined-cycle gas turbines, with natural gas as the main source of fuel. It is expected to become operational by the end of the century, the statement said.
Castle Peak Power Co Ltd, 60 percent owned by Exxon Energy and 40 percent by China Light, is involved in discussions about the resupply of gas to the Shenzhen project, it said.
China Light and Exxon have been in a joint venture in the power generation business in Hong Kong for more than 30 years.
"The Shenzhen project represents an extension of the two companies' cooperation outside Hong Kong," China Light said.
Shares of China Light ended HK$1.00 up at HK$34.50 on Thursday.
